text:
Leah (CS): heads up — RedTeak reported p99 latency spikes on their embeddings route starting ~08:10 UTC. They saw a bunch of 504s and some 2–3s tails. Ticket #RT-452 opened by their dev: https://redteak.example/t/RT-452.
Priya (Support): details from the customer: p95 ~180ms but p99 up to 2.4s, errors mostly when they send batched requests (batch_size ~ 64). They say it started after a morning traffic bump, no config changes on their side.
Nikhil (SRE): did we have any infra deploys around that time? checking.
infra-bot: deploys: none between 07:50–08:30 UTC. Autoscaler k8s-nodegroup spiked at 08:07 UTC, several pods restarted due to OOM on gpu-pool-2.
Jon (Eng-Platform): OOMs on gpu-pool-2 — looks like one tenant consumed a lot of memory/slots. Could be noisy neighbor. Any tenant IDs?
Leah (CS): customer sent logs — they include tenant_id: redteak-prod and requests with x-client-ip 34.83.12.47. They also observed higher queue times on their routes.
Priya (Support): repro steps from customer: 1) send 100 concurrent batched embed requests (bs=64) 2) observe 504s and long tails 3) if they space requests out latency returns to normal.
Nikhil (SRE): initial triage: per-tenant token bucket reached throttle briefly (we returned 429s) but the latency events are mainly 504/timeouts from the inference workers queueing. Correlation with OOMs suggests memory pressure.
Jon (Eng-Platform): short-term mitigation options: - add RedTeak tenant to temporary allowlist for burst capacity (only for their reserved pool) - pin their traffic to a smaller batch configuration (bs=8) via route override - scale up gpu-pool-2 nodes (manual)
Priya (Support): customer asked for an allowlist so their bursts don't hit tenant-level throttles. They requested immediate relief and asked for timeline.
Nikhil (SRE): I can do a targeted allowlist for their tenant_id on the throttle controller. Will do a conservative window (10 minutes) and monitor. Also enabling a per-tenant queue cap to prevent single tenant eviction of others.
Jon (Eng-Platform): can we also set a temporary route config for redteak-prod to `max_batch=8, max_concurrency=6`? that should reduce memory and avoid OOM. If we do that, add an automated rollback in 30m.
Leah (CS): customer agreed to lower batch size as a test. Priya — please confirm with them and ask for permission to route them to allowlist+reconfig.
Priya (Support): confirmed, customer provided OK. Executing steps now.
infra-bot: action: throttle-allowlist add tenant=redteak-prod duration=10m by=Nikhil (SRE) — success.
infra-bot: action: route-override apply tenant=redteak-prod config="max_batch=8,max_concurrency=6,rollback=30m" by=Jon (Eng-Platform) — success.
Nikhil (SRE): monitoring p95/p99 for their tenant and gpu-pool-2. Initial metrics: p95 reduced to ~160ms within 2 minutes; p99 down from 2.4s to ~480ms. Pod memory pressure reduced, OOMs stopped.
Leah (CS): customer reports far fewer timeouts, thanks team. They asked for a permanent fix — leaning on us to provide a longer-term allowlist or dedicated capacity.
Jon (Eng-Platform): next steps: create an incident follow-up runbook: - analyze which tenant caused the noisy behavior (search other tenants with high GPU mem allocations around 08:00) - consider per-tenant memory reservations and stricter queue caps - propose a pricing/contract for reserved bursts or Dedicated capacity - add automated detection for sudden batch-size-increase patterns in client traffic
Nikhil (SRE): I've started an investigation ticket: INF-983. Early signal shows another tenant (marigold-ops) had a sustained increase in concurrent batch size at 07:58 UTC — we need to correlate logs.
Priya (Support): putting a timeline in RT-452 and recommending Dedicated or a formal allowlist window while we complete infra changes.
Leah (CS): thanks. Can Eng-Platform estimate cost/time for per-tenant reservation work? Customer is sensitive to SLA.
Jon (Eng-Platform): quick estimate: config-first approach (queue caps + throttle tuning + detection rules) ~3–4 engineer-days, Dedicated offering migration depends on sales/ops. I'll draft the follow-up doc.
Nikhil (SRE): monitoring alert set: alert if p99 > 1s for any tenant for >5m and if gpu-pod OOM rate > 0.5/min across pool.
Leah (CS): perfect. Priya — please update the customer with the temporary mitigations and the planned follow-up. I'll mark this as resolved for now but keep INF-983 open until root cause is confirmed. :thumbsup:
Priya (Support): updated RT-452 with changes and asked customer for permission to keep an allowlist window overnight if needed.
infra-bot: note: all temporary configs will auto-rollback as scheduled.
Leah (CS): closing thread here, will reopen if anything pops back up. Thanks everyone.
